title: Slavery Abolition Act
summary: Britain's Parliament abolished slavery in most of the British Empire from 1 August 1834. About 800,000 people were freed, but most were bound as 'apprentices' until 1838-1840; East India Company territories, Ceylon and St Helena were excluded.
why: Slave-owners, not the enslaved, were paid £20 million in compensation, about 40% of the Treasury's annual income in 1833.

notes.problem: Presented abolition as a straightforward liberation; omitted compensation to slave-owners (not the enslaved), forced apprenticeship and excluded territories.
